quickAddParse.label: Quick add parsing
quickAddParse.description: Turns one sentence into a title, an owner, a deadline, an importance and labels. Today's date is supplied, so “tomorrow” and “by Friday” land on the right day.
quickAddParse.where: The quick add row on the board and in the personal workspace.
quickAddParse.example: “Give Nodira the quarterly report by Friday, urgent” → title, owner Nodira Karimova, deadline 19 September, urgent.

subtaskBreakdown.label: Break into steps
subtaskBreakdown.description: Splits one card into steps someone can actually do, each with a rough time.
subtaskBreakdown.where: The checklist section inside a card, and the personal workspace row.
subtaskBreakdown.example: “Prepare the EGDI package” → gather data, draft the schedule, agree with the unit, final copy.

planSprint.label: Plan the period
planSprint.description: Orders your open work by deadline, importance and the time you have left, says what to start with and what will not fit.
planSprint.where: Periods in the personal workspace, and the project page.
planSprint.example: Three hours and seven items → an ordered plan, the first one marked, two flagged as not fitting.

deadlineRisk.label: Explain this risk
deadlineRisk.description: Says in plain words why a card carries its risk badge and proposes one concrete step. It never recalculates the risk level.
deadlineRisk.where: Next to the risk badge on a card.
deadlineRisk.example: “The deadline passed yesterday and the checklist is half done” → the reason, plus “move the deadline to 22 September”.

catchUp.label: What did I miss
catchUp.description: Gathers what happened while you were away, or over the past week: finished work, risks, what is waiting for you. For the head it is the Monday briefing over the whole unit.
catchUp.where: Home, the personal workspace, and the project page.
catchUp.example: “Since Friday: 4 finished, 2 overdue, Anvar has 11 open items.”

draftEvent.label: Draft an event
draftEvent.description: Turns a one-line idea into a complete event: description, date options, a preparation checklist and a travel plan.
draftEvent.example: “Autumn outing to Chorvoq” → description, three date options, an eight-item checklist, a travel plan.

summarizeThread.label: Summarise the discussion
summarizeThread.description: Pulls the decisions, the open questions and who promised what out of a long comment thread, each with a link to the comment.
summarizeThread.example: 24 comments → 3 decisions, 2 open questions, “Anvar sends the PDF by Thursday”.

nlAnalytics.label: Ask analytics
nlAnalytics.description: Turns a plain-language question into a filter and answers with the numbers, showing the filter it used.
nlAnalytics.example: “Overdue work in the Data unit this month” → 7, with the filter and a chart.

translate.label: Translate
translate.description: Translates text into the language you pick, leaving department terms alone. Latin ↔ Cyrillic never goes to the model — it is converted here.
translate.where: Card description, the page editor, and personal notes.
translate.example: An Uzbek description → a Russian translation with “muddat” and “boʻlim” preserved.

draftReply.label: Draft a reply
draftReply.description: Writes a polite, businesslike reply to a discussion. It never sends: the text lands in the comment box and sending stays your decision.
draftReply.where: The card comment box, and a mention in the inbox.
draftReply.example: “Should I ask to move the deadline?” → a ready reply, plus “you still need to give the new date”.

boardRiskDigest.label: Who is running late
boardRiskDigest.description: Ranks the riskiest work on the board in a single call, each with a reason and one action. Head only.
boardRiskDigest.example: Five items with reasons, plus the pressure point “Anvar has 11 open items”.

suggestAssignee.label: Who should take this
suggestAssignee.description: Proposes three candidates by workload and experience. The reason is only ever workload or experience, never a judgement. The head chooses.
suggestAssignee.where: The owner field on a card.
suggestAssignee.example: “EGDI report” → Nodira (4 items on this subject), Anvar (heavily loaded), Dilnoza.

duplicateCheck.label: Find duplicates
duplicateCheck.description: While you write a new item, checks whether a similar one already exists and links to it.
duplicateCheck.where: Card creation, and the quick add preview.
duplicateCheck.example: “Prepare the report” → “Prepare the quarterly report” is already open.

semanticAsk.label: Ask the department's own records
semanticAsk.description: Answers a question using only this department's cards, comments, pages and events, citing each source. If it is not there, it says so.
semanticAsk.where: The “Ask” section on the AI page, and Ctrl+K.
semanticAsk.example: “Who is preparing the EGDI package?” → “Nodira Karimova, deadline 18 September”, linked to the card.
